_comment: Phase 7.1 data model. object_id cross-references data/items.json (indices 25-43, the 'scenery_or_character' category) so the engine's own per-turn L() locations tell us where a character currently is, at runtime, with no engine changes. Two entries (speaking-stone, dactyl) have no object_id -- they're room features, not objects in the noun table -- so they carry room_id instead. reveal_after: {"any_room_visited": [...]} gates on a fixed room list (used for the two room-bound entries, plus boatman/omegan where the book ties them to a specific first-encounter room); {"seen_object": true} gates on the object_id having appeared in any room the player has actually stood in, computed at runtime from the engine's own per-turn state -- no engine changes needed either way. book_caption values are original paraphrases of the book's character notes, not transcriptions -- see NOTICE.md.

characters.name: The Boatman
characters.book_caption: Even the fearless canyon beasts keep their distance from him -- take care. Still, you'll probably need to deal with him at some point.
characters.story_role: Ferries the player onward to room 57 once wisdom is high enough (X>=60); a low-wisdom approach leads to a bad ending (enslaved). See subroutine 1010-1070 in docs/semantics.md.

characters.name: Omegan
characters.book_caption: He roams his castle, so there's no telling where you'll run into him.
characters.story_role: The tragic center of the whole backstory: the one Earthling ever sent to Sky Land, given the Cloak of Entropy and a life-extension secret by the Sky People, tasked with collecting the hidden objects after the war -- and chose to hoard the Cloak's power instead. See the story panels in data/lore.json.

characters.name: Speaking Stone
characters.book_caption: For something called the Speaking Stone, this odd glassy boulder is remarkably quiet.
characters.story_role: The Clashing Stones inscription is the puzzle clue for waking it -- explains why H$ gets reused as the message "STONY WORDS" once seeding is done (docs/semantics.md).

characters.name: Swampman
characters.book_caption: He dwells among the stumps of the great bluewood trees his forebears planted. He hates the Logmen, but can't leave the swamp to take revenge -- or to fetch the liquor he thinks could bring the trees back to life.
characters.story_role: Wants the Logmen's liquor (object 31, "a still of bubbling green liquor") to restore the bluewood trees.

characters.name: The Logmen
characters.book_caption: A surly bunch always looking for amusement, hooked on a ferociously strong liquor of their own brewing. Their logging is wiping out the last bluewood trees in the east.
characters.story_role: Swampman's sworn enemies; the danger cutscene (thrown in water / tied up) is subroutine 1230-1300.

characters.name: Median
characters.book_caption: A renowned scholar of Ancient times who vanished in mysterious circumstances.
characters.story_role: Story panel 11: a wanderer who entered the Castle of Secrets long before Alphan, drew a plan, sealed it in a bottle and threw it into the Lake. The book strongly implies he and the amnesiac Scavenger are the same person.

characters.name: The Scavenger
characters.book_caption: He seems to have lost his memory, and Alphan will have to find some way to help him get it back.
characters.story_role: Likely Median, post-transformation and memory loss. The Sage of the Lilies' lilies are said to bring back lost memories -- probable connection worth confirming against the listing.

characters.name: Sage of the Lilies
characters.book_caption: She has meditated so long that only her head still moves. For centuries a small, nagging itch on her back has bothered her. The lilies in her care are said to bring back lost memories.
characters.story_role: The "irritation on her back" is a strong hint toward an item interaction; her lilies plausibly connect to the Scavenger's memory loss.

characters.name: Dactyl
characters.book_caption: She is guarding something valuable, and won't cooperate until you prove you're serious about your quest.
characters.story_role: A give-the-right-thing gate, guarding something at her nest.

characters.name: Canyon Beast
characters.book_caption: Canyon beasts turn up all over the forest, but you'll need help to catch one.
characters.story_role: Tameable/rideable once an enabling condition is met -- subroutine 1710-1720, "RIDE (tamed canyon beast)".
